mbm-0643.clue: I wait for the flute to take a breath.
mbm-0643.quote: In our choro circle I play cavaquinho beside a flutist who never seems to run out of air. When I finally hear a breath, I tuck in a little answering phrase. Last Sunday I got a smile around the mouthpiece.

mbm-0644.clue: I stage-manage with a tin of buttons.
mbm-0644.quote: The princess's shoe came apart before her entrance. I found two black buttons and a bit of elastic in my kit. She wore the repaired shoe for the whole run, and the cobbler in the audience never noticed.

mbm-0645.clue: I go back for the bicycle bell.
mbm-0645.quote: The museum has my city's first delivery tricycle, bell and all. The curator played me a recording of it. My corner grocer still rings a bell that sounds exactly like groceries coming home.

mbm-0646.clue: I climb for the orange handhold.
mbm-0646.quote: At the indoor wall I spent three evenings failing to reach the orange hold. On the fourth I touched it, laughed, and forgot what came next. That's as high as I've ever been while laughing.

mbm-0647.clue: I sew sleeves for a pair of elbows.
mbm-0647.quote: My friend plays cello in a jacket that wore through both elbows. I patched them in midnight blue velvet. When she plays a long note in stage light, the patches turn silver.

mbm-0648.clue: I learned my solo from a tailor.
mbm-0648.quote: The high phrase gave me trouble until the tailor in our choir drew a length of thread slowly through the air. I sang the whole line with my eyes on that hand. Next rehearsal the tailor brought a whole spool.

mbm-0649.clue: I keep the sand in my shoe.
mbm-0649.quote: I holed out of a bunker for the first time and came home with half the bunker in my left shoe. I shook it outside the next morning. That's quite enough reliving a golf shot.

mbm-0650.clue: I learned my first turn beside a wardrobe.
mbm-0650.quote: The wardrobe mirror only showed us from the knees down. By the time we reached a real ballroom, our feet knew the turn and our faces looked completely astonished.

mbm-0651.clue: I put my brother's plaid on the back.
mbm-0651.quote: His shirt didn't go with any square on the front. I pieced it into the quilt backing. When he turned it over, he knew the shirt by the little bleach moon on its pocket.

mbm-0652.clue: I count empty freight cars by their echoes.
mbm-0652.quote: Where the branch line crosses the underpass, empty wagons make a hollow boom. I tally them on my fingers. Once my train took so long to pass I had to borrow a friend's hands.

mbm-0653.clue: I watch the birds in the ticket queue.
mbm-0653.quote: Sparrows at our bus station dust-bathe under the timetable. I missed the express once watching one wriggle all the way onto its back. The local got me home smiling.

mbm-0654.clue: I carry a stone in my pocket uphill.
mbm-0654.quote: Dad used that little smooth pebble as a worry stone. At the top I take it out and let it warm up in the sun before we head down. He'd have liked the view.

mbm-0655.clue: I make bowls for rolling oranges.
mbm-0655.quote: My first fruit bowl had a wobble. An orange rolled round it without ever spilling out. I gave it a shallow spiral on purpose the next time and my nieces provide the oranges.

mbm-0656.clue: I curl with the broom that squeaks.
mbm-0656.quote: The handle on my old broom gives one little squeak when I sweep hard enough. My skip heard it over an entire rink during our first bonspiel. He calls it our extra teammate.

mbm-0657.clue: I mark my golf ball with a plum.
mbm-0657.quote: I dab on a purple dot and add one green line for the stem. Last week a child found my ball near the practice green and brought it back cupped like a tiny real fruit.

mbm-0658.clue: I have a book for short journeys.
mbm-0658.quote: It's an anthology of stories so short I can finish one between tram stops. I missed mine the day I found two stories arguing with each other on facing pages.

mbm-0659.clue: I keep the tape measure from a cake.
mbm-0659.quote: I made my niece a fabric birthday crown. She insisted on measuring the cake as well as her head, so I sewed a matching band for the cake stand. The cake wore hers sideways.

mbm-0660.clue: I make one saucer for the rain.
mbm-0660.quote: Every time I fire a set I leave a spare saucer on the balcony. Seeing the glaze through a skin of rain tells me more than the kiln light ever did.

mbm-0661.quote: My aunt wanted the front of her old dress in a quilt, but the buttons jabbed your chin. I stitched them to a little matching pouch. Now she can tell the story with one in her palm.

mbm-0662.clue: I serve toward the crooked palm tree.
mbm-0662.quote: At our beach court that palm tips far enough over the end line to shade one shoe. I serve from that cool spot. The ball never seems to mind going out into the heat.

mbm-0663.clue: I replay the underwater level for the bass.
mbm-0663.quote: My old game has four colors and a bass line that sounds like a cupboard shutting underwater. I can get through the whole stage on one life now. I still turn the volume up.

mbm-0664.clue: I take the patch of yellow as my cue.
mbm-0664.quote: From under canopy our drop zone looks like a green napkin with a yellow patchwork corner. The first time my folks came to watch they wore yellow too. I spotted them after I landed.

mbm-0665.clue: I tap the sand out before I climb.
mbm-0665.quote: I got sand in my shoes before my first outdoor climb and spent the morning blaming the rock. My climbing partner makes me tell that story every time we empty them now.

mbm-0666.clue: I went hiking for a gate that sings.
mbm-0666.quote: At the trail's last pasture the gate makes a high note on the way in and a low one leaving. I took the long way round just to hear the other half of its song.

mbm-0667.clue: I dance beside the old mirror ball.
mbm-0667.quote: The club retired its mirror ball to the corner where nobody used to dance. Then a little spot hit it and a hundred white squares ran across our shoes. It's the busiest corner now.
